design.text: Randomized, double-blind; ERAXIS 200 mg loading then 100 mg maintenance once daily IV vs IV fluconazole 800 mg loading then 400 mg maintenance; stratified by APACHE II score and presence/absence of neutropenia

citations.quote: Patients were randomized to receive once daily IV ERAXIS (200 mg loading dose followed by 100 mg

maintenance dose) or IV fluconazole (800 mg loading dose followed by 400 mg maintenance dose). Patients were stratified by APACHE II score (\le 20 and > 20) and the presence or absence of neutropenia.

population.text: Patients with candidemia and/or other forms of invasive candidiasis; patients with Candida endocarditis, osteomyelitis or meningitis or C. krusei infection excluded

citations.quote: Patients with *Candida* endocarditis, osteomyelitis or meningitis, or those with infection due to *C. krusei*, were excluded from the study.

endpoint.text: Primary analysis of global response at the end of IV therapy in the modified intent-to-treat (MITT) population; successful global response required clinical cure/improvement plus documented or presumed microbiological eradication

citations.quote: Patients who received at least one dose of study medication and who had a positive culture for *Candida* species from a normally sterile site before entry into the study (modified intent-to-treat [MITT] population) were included in the primary analysis of global response at the end of IV therapy. A successful global response required clinical cure or improvement (significant, but incomplete resolution of signs and symptoms of the *Candida* infection and no additional antifungal treatment), and documented or presumed microbiological eradication. Patients with an indeterminate outcome were analyzed as failures in this population.

design.text: Double-blind, double-dummy, randomized; ERAXIS 100 mg loading IV Day 1 then 50 mg/day IV vs oral fluconazole 200 mg loading then 100 mg/day; treatment 7 days beyond symptom resolution (min 14, max 21 days)

citations.quote: Three hundred patients received ERAXIS (100 mg loading dose IV on Day 1 followed by 50 mg/day IV) and 301 received oral fluconazole (200 mg loading dose on Day 1 followed by 100 mg/day). Treatment duration was 7 days beyond resolution of symptoms for a minimum of 14 and a maximum of 21 days.

endpoint.text: Endoscopic outcome (endoscopic success = cure or improvement) at end of therapy in the clinically evaluable population

citations.quote: The primary endpoint was endoscopic outcome at end of therapy (EOT).

n.text: 601 treated (300 ERAXIS, 301 fluconazole); clinically evaluable population 231 anidulafungin, 236 fluconazole

citations.quote: Three hundred patients received ERAXIS (100 mg loading dose IV on Day 1 followed by 50 mg/day IV) and 301 received oral fluconazole (200 mg loading dose on Day 1 followed by 100 mg/day). Treatment duration was 7 days beyond resolution of symptoms for a minimum of 14 and a maximum of 21 days.

An endoscopic success, defined as cure (endoscopic grade of 0 on a 4 point severity scale) or improvement (decrease of one or more grades from baseline), was seen in 225/231 (97.4%) anidulafungin-treated patients and 233/236 (98.7%) fluconazole-treated patients (Table 7).

result.text: Endoscopic success at EOT: ERAXIS 225/231 (97.4%) vs fluconazole 233/236 (98.7%); difference -1.3% (95% CI -3.8%, 1.2%). Higher endoscopic relapse 2 weeks post-treatment: 120/225 (53.3%) anidulafungin vs 45/233 (19.3%) fluconazole

indication.text: ERAXIS is indicated for treatment of candidemia and other forms of Candida infections (intra-abdominal abscess and peritonitis) and esophageal candidiasis

Esophageal candidiasis (see CLINICAL STUDIES, Table 7 for higher relapse rates off anidulafungin therapy)

target_moa.text: Anidulafungin is a semi-synthetic echinocandin that inhibits glucan synthase (present in fungal but not mammalian cells), inhibiting formation of 1,3-β-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall

citations.quote: Anidulafungin is a semi-synthetic echinocandin with antifungal activity. Anidulafungin inhibits glucan synthase, an enzyme present in fungal, but not mammalian cells. This results in inhibition of the formation of 1,3-\beta-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall.

ERAXIS (anidulafungin) is a semi-synthetic lipopeptide synthesized from a fermentation product of *Aspergillus nidulans*. Anidulafungin is an echinocandin, a class of antifungal drugs that inhibits the synthesis of 1,3-\beta-D-glucan, an essential component of fungal cell walls.

key_safety.text: Overall ERAXIS safety assessed in 929 individuals. In candidemia, treatment-related AEs reported in >=2.0% of subjects: at least 1 treatment-related AE 24.4% vs fluconazole 26.4%; diarrhea 3.1%, hypokalemia 3.1%. Possible histamine-mediated symptoms (rash, urticaria, flushing, pruritus, dyspnea, hypotension) reported. Hepatic effects: laboratory abnormalities in liver function tests seen in volunteers and patients

summary.text: ERAXIS (anidulafungin) NDA 21-632 was originally submitted April 25, 2003, received approvable letters in 2004 and 2005, and was approved on the date of this 2006 letter for esophageal candidiasis, together with NDA 21-948 for candidemia and other Candida infections; a deferred pediatric study was required as a postmarketing commitment under PREA

citations.quote: NDA 21-632, originally submitted on April 25, 2003, received an approvable letter on May 21, 2004.

NDA 21-948 was submitted on August 18, 2005 and received on August 18, 2005. This new drug application provides for the use of Eraxis (anidulafungin) for Injection for the treatment of patients with candidemia and other forms of *Candida* infections (intra-abdominal abscess and peritonitis).
We completed our review of these applications, as amended. They are approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the agreed-upon labeling text.
Your deferred pediatric studies required under section 2 of the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) are considered required postmarketing study commitments.
